We show that the sample SIR eigenvalues exhibit an upward bias when $\gamma>0$, that their fluctuations are governed by the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble, and that the signal eigenvalues are asymptotically normal after an appropriate bias correction. We demonstrate that Li's chi-squared test requires a scaling adjustment to achieve the nominal asymptotic size when $\gamma>0$. We further propose two additional tests that achieve the nominal asymptotic size: an exact test based on Li's test statistic and a largest-eigenvalue test. In addition, we derive closed-form limits for the accuracy of the estimated SIR directions and show that their first-order expansions in $\gamma$ agree with Li's approximation. Finally, we establish the limiting distribution of the estimated sufficient predictors for a new observation and show that, when $\gamma>0$, they contain an additional independent Gaussian noise component. Simulation studies corroborate our theoretical findings.

nominations.title: Conformal prediction for censored life history data
nominations.authors: Lu Mao
nominations.abstract: We consider individual prediction of general summaries of a multistate trajectory, such as time alive out of hospital or time spent in remission. Right censoring complicates calibration because these outcomes may be only partially observed. We develop a conformal prediction approach for scalar and vector summaries over a fixed clinical horizon supported by follow-up. For each candidate region, we define the coverage determining time as the earliest time at which the observed history establishes whether the outcome lies in the region, even if the outcome itself is still unknown. We weight observed coverage decisions by the inverse probability of remaining uncensored to that time and augment the estimator with conditional coverage probabilities for unresolved histories. For a fixed region, the coverage estimator is doubly robust with respect to the censoring and conditional coverage models and attains the semiparametric efficiency bound when both are consistent at suitable rates. For the calibrated region, we derive a finite-sample lower bound on the coverage probability and establish asymptotic validity if either model is correct. In simulations, using partial histories yields narrower prediction intervals at comparable coverage. We illustrate joint prediction of days in and out of hospital in the HF-ACTION trial and prediction of relapse-free time in the German Breast Cancer Study Group cohort.

nominations.title: Two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems for high-dimensional data: noncentral normal-reference inference
nominations.authors: Pengfei Wang
nominations.abstract: We study noncentral normal-reference inference for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems. Within the Gaussian reference, a shifted null law is accurate if and only if covariance-weighted signal energy is negligible relative to the trace of the squared covariance. We establish the sharp uniform fourth-root error order over unrestricted spectra and a linear bound under spectral spread. A separate spectral-range criterion determines when signal magnitude alone suffices. An augmented spherical reference gives finite-sample calibration for Gaussian samples and asymptotically recovers Gaussian-reference local power under projection fourth-moment bounds and control of diagonal fluctuations, without a dimension-to-sample-size restriction. For unknown Gaussian covariance, explicit trace and hollow-Gram confidence bounds turn the linear approximation bound into a simultaneous, computable certificate over local effect ranges. Eigenspace signal energies describe directional power, while a two-point argument limits estimation of unknown local power. Simulations with 10,000 evaluation replications per configuration examine unequal and noncommuting covariances, severe sample imbalance, non-Gaussian observations and the informativeness of the certificate.

nominations.title: The exact region of the Average Rectangular Volume and Spearman's rho, with an application to arachnitude
nominations.authors: Luca Anzilli, Fabrizio Durante
nominations.abstract: The average rectangular volume ($\ARV$) of a bivariate aggregation function is the average of its volumes over all axis-parallel rectangles of the unit square; for a copula, it is the expected copula volume of the rectangle spanned by two independent uniform points. We determine the exact region of the pairs $(\ARV(C),\rho(C))$, where $C$ ranges over all bivariate copulas and $\rho$ is Spearman's rho. The region is compact, convex and symmetric, and its upper boundary consists of three analytically parametrized arcs. A previously proposed family of shuffles of Min generates one arc, but only on part of its range; the other two arcs are generated by singular copulas whose supports contain hyperbolic branches. The boundary is continuously differentiable away from its left endpoint $\ARV=\frac{11}{120}$, where it has a vertical tangent. The proof uses a folding transformation and explicit Kantorovich potentials for a family of optimal transport problems. Finally, we show that the arachnitude, a rank correlation used in actuarial practice, is an affine transformation of $\ARV$, so that the result also describes the joint region of Spearman's rho and arachnitude.

nominations.title: Fundamental Limits of Honest Inference with Heterogeneous Transfer Sources
nominations.authors: Xuran Meng, Yi Li
nominations.abstract: Transfer learning can improve precision by borrowing information from external sources, but how much improvement is possible while maintaining valid inference? We address this by studying honest confidence intervals for a target parameter using multiple sources with heterogeneous prespecified discrepancy bounds. Under local information and admissibility conditions, we establish a universal lower bound on interval length for procedures maintaining uniform coverage. A scalar information equation characterizes the bound, revealing how precision depends jointly on source sample sizes and discrepancies. Large source samples need not yield greater precision gains when their discrepancies are large. When discrepancies are unrestricted, honest intervals cannot improve upon the target-only rate, even when all sources are unbiased. For the Gaussian location model, we calculate optimal source weights and construct honest intervals attaining the lower bound order, establishing sharpness. We extend the lower bound theory to semiparametric models through parametric submodels. For the Cox proportional hazards model, we verify the information conditions under which the lower bound applies, including under right censoring.

nominations.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
nominations.authors: Nikola Bani\'c, Neven Elezovi\'c
nominations.abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(\beta_c(n)=\beta_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(\gamma_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/\beta_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

nominations.title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
nominations.authors: Tania Roa, Meryem Slaoui, Soledad Torres
nominations.abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

nominations.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
nominations.authors: Thomas Stark, Georg K\"ostenberger, Nina D\"ornemann
nominations.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

nominations.title: Escaping the Curse of Dimensionality in One-Step Flow-Based Generative Models
nominations.authors: Konstantin Yakovlev
nominations.abstract: Flow and diffusion-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art quality, but require multiple forward passes at inference time, making them computationally costly. Consistency models overcome this by learning a flow map directly, enabling few-step generation and dramatically reducing the computation needed at test time. However, formal statistical guarantees for such one-step generators are scarce. Existing results either suffer from the curse of dimensionality or rely on impractical loss functions. We investigate whether one-step flow-based models can escape the curse of dimensionality under the assumption that the data distribution is generated by a low-dimensional surface perturbed with Gaussian noise. In this setup, we derive approximation and generalization error bounds for the flow map estimate that circumvent the curse of dimensionality. Our findings provide the first principled explanation for practical success of one-step flow-based generative models.

nominations.title: Statistical-to-computational gaps in central limit theorems for high-dimensional tensors
nominations.authors: Debsurya De, Dmitriy Kunisky
nominations.abstract: We study high-dimensional central limit theorems (CLTs) as hypothesis testing problems, comparing the number of summands needed for statistical and computational indistinguishability of the normalized sum from the limiting Gaussian distribution as the dimension and number of summands grow together. For the off-diagonal entries of sums of i.i.d. rank-one tensors formed from standard Gaussian vectors (equivalently, the problem of distinguishing Wigner from Wishart tensors), we prove total variation bounds sharpening previous estimates of Mikulincer (2020) and give matching polynomial-time tests. This shows that the statistical and computational thresholds coincide for this CLT, contrary to a proposal by Kunisky, Moore, and Wein (2024). On the other hand, we also show that, for tensors of order at least three, sufficient Gaussian dilution of the summands by adding independent Gaussian noise and rescaling gives a CLT model with a statistical-to-computational gap (in the above setting and ones with more general rank-one summand distributions). To the best of our knowledge, such a phenomenon has not been observed before in any high-dimensional CLT. In particular, in the relevant parameter regimes, we show that a brute-force search achieves strong detection, while polynomials of degree up to $n^{\Omega(1)}$ cannot achieve strong separation. The latter lower bounds control low-degree $\chi^2$-divergences by a novel method based on cumulant generating functions, and we further illustrate the use of these tools by applying them to masked tensor CLT models where only a prescribed subset of tensor entries is revealed.

nominations.title: Beyond Curvature Bias: Higher-Order Manifold Fitting via Multiscale Cancellation
nominations.authors: Zhijun Zhu, Haoyu Yang, Ruoyu Xiong, Bingjie Li, Zhigang Yao
nominations.abstract: Local manifold-fitting procedures smooth noisy observations over neighborhoods of scale $h$, inducing a systematic normal bias of order $h^2+\sigma^2$ that persists at the population level. We develop geometric bias cancellation (GBC), a multiscale framework for higher-order manifold recovery under ambient Gaussian noise. For procedures admitting a normal-bias expansion $c(h,\sigma)b(x)+O(h^4)$, we construct cross-scale correspondence using estimated normal fibers and show that second-order normal accuracy suffices for fourth-order correspondence accuracy. Canceling the leading geometric bias yields $O(h^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy while preserving an embedded manifold diffeomorphic to the underlying manifold. We establish the required expansions and finite-sample recovery guarantees for successive tangent-space projection and Gaussian density ridges. For STSP, geometric bias cancellation also achieves an asymptotically vanishing Hausdorff error ratio relative to oracle bandwidth-tuned single-scale fitting. For the local contraction estimator of \citet{yao2023manifold}, we identify an obstruction to scalar bias cancellation and develop a directional cancellation achieving $O(\sigma^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy with uniform positive reach, as well as fourth-order finite-sample accuracy when $n\gtrsim\sigma^{-(d+6)}\log(1/\sigma)$. Simulations confirm the predicted improvement from second- to fourth-order population bias.

nominations.title: Posterior contraction rates for banded approximations of Gaussian processes
nominations.authors: Omar Kassi, Bernhard Stankewitz, Botond Szabo
nominations.abstract: Gaussian process regression models are widely used in modern statistics and machine learning due to their flexibility, interpretability, built-in uncertainty quantification, and strong theoretical foundations. However, training Gaussian processes (GPs) has a computational cost of $O(n^3)$, while the memory and prediction costs are also $O(n^2)$. For large datasets commonly encountered in practice, this becomes infeasible and necessitates the use of approximate posterior methods. In this work, we propose a class of approximations based on sparse covariance matrices, where the kernel matrix is sparsified according to the spatial proximity of the design points. We analyze the accuracy of the resulting approximate posterior distribution and show that the proposed approach preserves optimal statistical inference properties, provided that the dependencies among a sufficient number of neighboring points for each feature are retained. We derive explicit sufficient and necessary conditions on the number of neighbors required in a general setting and apply these results to standard kernels, including the squared exponential and Mat\'ern kernels. Our theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments.

nominations.title: Parameter estimation in models with explosive drift and Gaussian noise
nominations.authors: Yuliya Mishura, Kostiantyn Ralchenko, Mykyta Yakovliev
nominations.abstract: We study drift parameter estimation for a positive stochastic process with singular mean-reverting drift driven by Gaussian noise. For Riemann-Liouville fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$, an observable fractional transformation reduces the model to a semimartingale with drift linear in the unknown parameters. Using the quasi-likelihood approach, we derive explicit estimators of both drift coefficients. For a broader class of Gaussian driving processes, we construct a strongly consistent estimator of the ratio $a/b$, which has a natural mean-reversion interpretation, and verify the required assumptions for several Gaussian models. The theoretical results are complemented by a simulation study investigating the effects of the observation horizon and the discretization step on the finite-sample accuracy of the proposed estimators.

nominations.title: Automatic Threshold Selection Leaves Finite-Degree Bias in Network Power-Law Fits
nominations.authors: Tiandong Wang
nominations.abstract: Minimum-distance fitting selects a degree threshold and a power-law exponent from the same network. We study the procedure that fits a continuous Pareto law with the Hill estimator and minimizes the Kolmogorov--Smirnov distance over retained ranks. For homogeneous linear preferential attachment and Norros--Reittu graphs with Pareto weights, we derive the joint limiting law of the selected rank, retained fraction of the threshold tie, and exponent error. The selector retains of order $n^{2/(\alpha+2)}$ of $n$ vertices, where $\alpha$ is the survival exponent. At this rank, integer spacing and finite-degree departures from a Pareto tail have the same order as sampling fluctuations. The exponent estimate is consistent and retains a shift on the scale used for confidence intervals. For integer degree laws whose tail sums have a first-order inverse-degree expansion, adding the retained tie fraction divided by the threshold to the Hill statistic removes the leading contribution of the tie. Under homogeneous preferential attachment with a fixed known number of edges per new vertex, removing the remaining model-specific term and calibrating for selection gives confidence intervals with asymptotically exact coverage. Observed networks show sensitivity of the fitted exponent and the classification of degree variance to threshold ties. Simulations assess interval coverage and show improved pooled connectivity predictions after correction under both specified graph laws. Changes to the Norros--Reittu weight distribution can reverse the prediction gain.

nominations.title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
nominations.authors: Louison Bocquet-Nouaille, J\'er\^ome Morio, Benjamin Bobbia, Philippe Naveau
nominations.abstract: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

nominations.title: Isotonic least squares is robust to heteroscedasticity, unimodal least squares is not
nominations.authors: Yannick Baraud
nominations.abstract: We compare the least squares estimator (LSE) with the $\ell_{1}$-estimator recently introduced by Baraud and Maillard~\citeyearpar{BM-2026} for estimating a regression function under a fixed design, when the errors are independent but possibly heteroscedastic and heavy-tailed. We show that the two estimators coincide on the class of nondecreasing (or nonincreasing) functions on an interval. As a consequence, the isotonic LSE inherits the non-asymptotic $\ell_{1}$-risk bounds of the $\ell_{1}$-estimator, which only require a moment of order $p\in[1,2]$ on the errors and depend on the average of their $p$-th absolute moments rather than on their maximum. This coincidence no longer holds on the nonconvex class of unimodal functions: we exhibit a heteroscedastic Gaussian example in which the LSE is inconsistent while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator converges at the parametric rate. Finally, we show on a one-dimensional linear model that neither estimator dominates the other: depending on the way the noise is distributed among the design points, the LSE may converge at rate $1/n$ while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator is inconsistent.

nominations.title: Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time
nominations.authors: Felix Zhou
nominations.abstract: We revisit the problem of estimating $k$ linear regressors with self-selection bias in $n$ dimensions up to error $\varepsilon$ with the maximum self-selection criterion, as introduced by Cherapanamjeri, Daskalakis, Ilyas, and Zampetakis [CDIZ23, STOC]. Our main result is a $\mathrm{poly}(n,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time algorithm for the unknown-index variant of this problem, thereby improving upon the running times of the best known algorithms due to Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] and Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Zhou [KMZ26, COLT] with exponential dependence on $k$. Our algorithm succeeds in the presence of correlated noise between regressors, which captures the related setting of max-affine regression. Consequently, we also give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem, improving on the prior works of Ghosh, Pananjady, Guntuboyina, and Ramchandran [GPGR22, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory] and Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] with exponential dependence on $k$. Prior works exhaustively search over a $k$-dimensional subspace spanned by the regressors, using conditional moments of the response to test candidates. In contrast, our algorithm is driven by an improved understanding of the moments of the covariates. We show that, restricting to observations with large response values, the degree-$(\log n)$ Hermite moment of the covariates approximately decomposes as a sum of tensor powers of the regressors. The first step of our algorithm can be viewed as a tensor decomposition algorithm for these implicitly represented high-order tensors, which outputs unit vectors parallel to the regressors. A secondary step based on a simple variant of ordinary least squares extracts estimates for the regressors given these unit vectors. We believe our analytic insight and algorithmic components may have applications to designing efficient algorithms for other latent-variable problems.

nominations.title: Recent developments in spatial econometrics
nominations.authors: Abhimanyu Gupta
nominations.abstract: We conduct a non-exhaustive survey of the recent spatial econometrics literature by placing it in historical context and mapping current trends. The focus will be primarily on methodological aspects. Starting from the canonical spatial autoregressive model, we cover its many extensions and richer parameterizations. We discuss spatial panel data models and advancements in the study of nonlinear and nonparametric models. Specification testing for spatial econometric models, with its roots in the $J$-test of Davidson and MacKinnon (1981), is also covered, as is spatial correlation robust inference. Finally, we review advancements in general limit theory, limited dependent variable models, spatial weight matrix estimation and endogeneity, recent attempts at uniting the network formation and spatial literature, and sundry important topics. We take stock of the current paradigm and critically evaluate the impact of the spatial literature on applied practice.

nominations.title: Identification of Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models
nominations.authors: Dennis Kristensen, Ruolei Zhu
nominations.abstract: This paper introduces a novel class of econometric models, called Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models. It is based on the discrete choice rational inattention model of Matvejka and McKay (2015) with additive unobserved heterogeneity incorporated. We show that some of the systematic components of the primitives of the model are nonparametrically identified even if the distributions of unobserved variables and the prior of decision makers are both unknown to the Econometrician. If additional information about the prior is known to the Econometrician, even stronger identification results become available.

nominations.title: Lost in the Bins: Treatment Effects with Discretized Covariates
nominations.authors: Cenchen Liu
nominations.abstract: Mean independence restrictions are widely used to identify average treatment effects, but the covariates used to formulate these restrictions are often observed or used in coarsened form. This paper shows that mean independence conditional on a finely measured covariate need not hold after the covariate is replaced by a coarsened version. Coarsening can therefore change the identifying content of the comparison rather than only the precision of estimation. I characterize the resulting coarsening bias for the ATT and ATE. For the ATT, the bias is driven by within-cell composition in untreated potential outcomes. For the ATE, an additional treatment effect heterogeneity term appears. I then introduce $c$-mean dependence, a nonparametric relaxation of exact mean independence at the coarsened level, and derive sharp bounds for average treatment effects. The parameter $c$ determines how far comparisons may extend across neighboring values of the coarsened covariate. I propose sample analogue estimators and bootstrap inference procedures for the resulting bound functions. In an application to voluntary military service using data from Angrist (1998), positive effects on early earnings, which primarily reflect military pay, hold even under the weakest form of $c$-mean dependence, whereas the evidence on later effects on civilian earnings is inconclusive once mean independence is relaxed.

nominations.title: Inference After Model Refutation: Uniform Post-Relaxation Inference for Partially Identified Models
nominations.authors: Ulrich Hounyo
nominations.abstract: When data reject an econometric model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others, even when that inference is exact. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. With repair-by-repair primitive bounds, PR equals the union of all post-relaxation targets compatible with the band, so no smaller band-based set has the same guarantee. I derive limits on learning the repair, the exact perturbation radius of the minimal-repair correspondence, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and a reduced-form version valid at zero first stages. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument should be dropped, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect of institutions.

nominations.title: Introducing and Repealing an EV Subsidy: Evidence from New Zealand's Clean Car Discount
nominations.authors: Fabian Dunker, Jyotsna Garg
nominations.abstract: New Zealand's Clean Car Discount (CCD) was a feebate scheme that offered rebates for low-emission vehicles from July 2021, added fees for high-emission vehicles from April 2022, and was abolished at the end of December 2023. Shortly afterwards, road user charges were introduced for electric vehicles (EVs). We study how EV adoption responded to the introduction and the abrupt repeal of the scheme, using monthly vehicle registration data from 2014 to 2024. A structural break analysis following Bai and Perron, combined with a regression discontinuity in time, shows that breaks in the registrations of battery electric, plug-in hybrid and conventional vehicles coincide with the policy dates. To estimate causal effects, we apply a difference-in-differences approach with Queensland, Australia, as a comparison region and Newey-West standard errors. Because the New Zealand market was about four times larger, the analysis uses log-transformed registrations, so that parallel trends refer to equal growth rates. The results are asymmetric. After the introduction of the rebates, EV registrations in New Zealand rose strongly, but by a similar proportion as in Queensland, and the average effect relative to Queensland is not statistically significant. A specification allowing for a change in slope suggests a gradual acceleration of EV uptake. After the repeal, EV registrations fell by about 72% relative to Queensland, and the decline persisted in 2025. Both policy dates were preceded by a rush of purchases. The average CO2 emissions of newly registered vehicles fell markedly during the scheme and rebounded after its end. The results suggest that an abrupt end of EV purchase incentives can cause a large and lasting drop in EV uptake, and that a gradual, pre-announced phase-out may be preferable.

nominations.title: Testing Density Discontinuity Using Spacings
nominations.authors: William T. Firmin
nominations.abstract: In the regression discontinuity design, researchers assess the credibility of assumptions by testing the running variable's density for a discontinuity at the cutoff. This paper proposes a novel such test. The test uses q spacings on each side of the cutoff, where spacings are the widths between ordered observations. Spacings yield a continuous statistic that behaves well under weak assumptions. I study its properties in two asymptotic frameworks: one where q is fixed as the sample size increases and one where q slowly diverges to infinity. With q fixed, the test achieves exact asymptotic size control without user randomization. When q increases slowly, the test becomes consistent without sacrificing exact asymptotic size. Compared to the preferred version of Bugni and Canay's (2021) test, the only other test with comparably weak assumptions, this test reduces sensitivity to the tuning parameter and performs similarly when theirs is well-chosen.

nominations.title: Uniform Inference for Two-Way Clustered Data
nominations.authors: Ulrich Hounyo, Jiahao Lin, Xiaojun Song, Hansheng Wang
nominations.abstract: We establish uniformly asymptotically exact inference for the population mean of two-way clustered data, allowing the data-generating process to vary with sample size. This finding does not contradict the well-known impossibility result of Menzel (2021), which places a fundamental limit on uniform estimation of the asymptotic distribution of the normalized full-array mean. We estimate the same population mean by averaging the sample means from random matchings. A closed-form standard error makes the resulting confidence interval straightforward to implement. The variance estimator is positive semidefinite and the studentized matching estimator is uniformly asymptotically standard normal. The cost of uniform validity is a slower convergence rate under degeneracy. We extend the result to smooth functions of GMM parameters, allowing the different moment components to exhibit different dependence regimes. In simulations, the proposed confidence intervals achieve coverage close to the nominal level across the dependence regimes considered.

nominations.title: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age
nominations.authors: Caroline Chin, Shagun Kala, Nadav Kunievsky, Teng Liu, Alex Martin Richmond, Carl Shan
nominations.abstract: This paper examines how freelance work is changing in the AI era. We compare the activities people undertake in ChatGPT with the work clients request on Upwork, an online freelance platform, and examine how clients combine tasks into projects. We find that activities more prevalent in ChatGPT tend to lose marketplace share on Upwork, while those less prevalent tend to gain share. Within AI-related work, demand is becoming more diverse, and job postings combine tasks that were rarely requested together before the generative AI era. AI-related postings also have substantially larger project budgets and involve more hours of work, while differences in hourly rates are small. Together, these findings suggest that AI is reshaping not only which tasks clients outsource, but also how they combine tasks into larger, higher-value projects.

nominations.title: When Does a Recommendation Spark Curiosity? Theory, Measurement, and Field Evidence
nominations.authors: Pan Li, Alexander Tuzhilin
nominations.abstract: Curiosity, the drive to close the gap between what one knows and what one wants to know, pulls consumers beyond their familiar content, sustains engagement, and breaks them out of the filter bubbles of repetitive, relevance-only recommendations. Despite its importance, curiosity is hardly incorporated into modern recommender systems for lack of a formal measure. The information-gap theory of curiosity provides no formal quantitative model that a recommender system can operate on, and existing proxy metrics do not accurately measure the curiosity that a recommended item evokes. To fill this research gap, we formalize the information-gap theory into five axioms of curiosity and construct the canonical formulation of a computational measure of the curiosity that a recommended item evokes in a consumer. We validate our curiosity measure through a survey-based study, in which it matches consumers' self-reported curiosity and outperforms alternative proxy metrics. We subsequently build a curiosity-aware recommender system that incorporates this measure into the utility function design, and we show through offline experiments on three real-world datasets that it significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we conduct a large-scale online controlled experiment at a major video-streaming platform in Asia, where we show that our method significantly increases click-through rate, video views, and time spent over the latest production system, leading to tangible economic impact for the company. Our method has since been deployed on the platform and remains in operation. Our findings establish consumer curiosity as a measurable and actionable objective for recommender systems, with important managerial implications for digital platforms to recommend what consumers wonder about.

nominations.title: From the firm- to the application-level: A new typology of AI use in organisations
nominations.authors: Fulvio Castellacci
nominations.abstract: Artificial intelligence is applied in organisations in many different ways. However, the firm-level literature on AI lacks a conceptual framework able to describe that variety. Empirical studies typically examine one dimension of AI use at a time. This paper argues that the difficulty follows from the unit of analysis: a firm may hold many AI applications at once, each with its own novelty, sourcing mode, objective and technology type. These dimensions are defined at the level of the application rather than of the firm. We therefore propose shifting the unit of analysis from the firm to the individual AI application, and develop a typology combining these four conceptual dimensions. The new framework locates any application in a common space, and it points out in particular two types that the prevailing adoption-innovation distinction neglects: co-invention, novel uses of technology the firm did not develop, and internalisation, in-house building of AI that could have been bought instead. Documented use cases illustrate the framework, which is then used to discuss implications for firms strategies and the diffusion of AI in economic systems.

nominations.title: Factors Influencing Rural Female Workforce Participation in India, 2017- 2025: An Econometric Analysis Using District-Level Panel Data
nominations.authors: Bishwanath Goldar, Suresh Chand Aggarwal
nominations.abstract: Rural female workforce participation rate (RFWPR) in India declined between 1993-94 and 2017-18. After 2017-18, the trend reversed, and RFWPR rose from 23.7% in 2017-18 to 44.9% in 2025. Using district-level panel data for about 500 districts for nine years, 2017-18 to 2025, the paper analyzes econometrically some key determinants of RFWPR in India in the recent period. We find that the presence of young children in the family tends to reduce RFWPR, consistent with findings from several previous studies. Our econometric model results indicate that an increase in household real income, proxied by the monthly per capita consumption expenditure deflated by the consumer price index, tends to reduce RFWPR. Increases in the real wage rate of casual workers in rural areas, likely reflecting a shortage of such labour, particularly in agriculture, tend to raise RFWPR. However, the positive effect of wage hikes on RFWPR continues only until real rural wages reach a particular level. Beyond that wage rate, the positive effect of wages on RFWPR diminishes or could even turn negative, i.e., rural wage hikes tending to reduce RFWPR.

nominations.title: Huge If True: Learning from the Size of the Surprise
nominations.authors: Thomas Graeber, Christopher Roth, Marco Sammon, Constantin Schesch
nominations.abstract: Responses to earnings surprises depend on an unknown multiplier mapping earnings to value. Investors, however, learn about the news and the multiplier from the same number. Large surprises may indicate small multipliers and tiny surprises large ones. We model how greater uncertainty about the multiplier attenuates responses on average but makes them steeper near zero surprises. In an incentivized experiment, we find that greater processing constraints lower average sensitivity but raise it near zero. We confirm this with real-world earnings announcements: stocks with higher valuation uncertainty, our proxy for multiplier uncertainty, respond less on average but more steeply near zero.

nominations.title: Price co-movement and price information diverge across Nordic electricity zones after the energy crisis
nominations.authors: My Thi Diem Phan, Tuyen Trung Truong, Hoai Phuong Ha, Dat Thanh Nguyen
nominations.abstract: After the 2021-2022 energy crisis, day-ahead prices in Nordic bidding zones no longer move together. We ask whether this divergence also changes the information carried by prices. The answer matters for integrating variable renewable energy (VRE), because it can help identify where wind and solar forecasts are worth producing, publishing, and using. We measured the co-movement of each Norwegian and Swedish zone with Germany-Luxembourg (DE-LU) in 2018-2025. We then used a single model, selected on 2024 data, to forecast 2025 prices at 11:00 on the previous day and tested which inputs improved accuracy in each zone. The zones moved alike until 2019, but co-movement diverged in Sweden in 2020 and in Norway in 2021, and the split has persisted. In 2024, four southern zones co-moved strongly with DE-LU (intraday correlations of 0.54-0.71), while four northern zones co-moved weakly (0.25-0.30). Yet price information did not follow this split. Previous-day neighbouring prices reduced mean absolute error by at most 2.2% in any zone, equally in coupled and isolated zones. Removing the transmission system operators' wind and solar forecasts increased mean absolute error by at most 6% in Norway, 8-16% in Sweden, and 31% in DE-LU, and the ordering held in 2024. Within Norway, the value of these forecasts showed no detectable dependence on reservoir filling. The divergence in co-movement was therefore not matched by a divergence in price information, which differed mainly between national generation systems. Thus, a zone's coupling to the continent does not indicate the value of VRE forecasts there.

nominations.title: Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities
nominations.authors: Likun Cao
nominations.abstract: Research on pay dispersion has long asked whether unequal rewards increase or depress performance. Tournament theory expects stronger effort, while social comparison accounts expect withdrawal. Both perspectives, however, treat performance as a single scale on which workers can be ranked. Scientific work often resists such ordering. Some contributions extend recognized lines of inquiry and can be evaluated against prevailing standards; others revise the frames through which value is judged and become legible only later. We argue that intellectual tournaments more readily reward the first kind of contribution than the second. Pay dispersion may therefore be associated not only with how much scholars produce but also with what kinds of intellectual exploration are encouraged. We test this argument with administrative payroll records for 105,050 tenure-line faculty in 4,839 departments at 93 U.S. public universities from 2004 to 2026, linked to publication histories in OpenAlex. For each department, we estimate a separate pay equation using rank, contract basis, and seniority, then measure the Gini of the salary variation this local ladder cannot explain. Scholars in departments with greater unexplained pay dispersion publish more papers and receive more citations, but their work is less disruptive, less novel, and more conventional. Additional analyses show that compensation premiums above the ladder go disproportionately to scholars with broad collaborations and topical breadth. Although the design cannot fully separate treatment from selection, the evidence shows that inequality is not only a distributional outcome but also an evaluative structure, shaping which forms of knowledge are recognized, rewarded, and reproduced within organizations and communities.

nominations.title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
nominations.authors: Y. Zhu, K. Marlor, V. Lavelle, T. S. Brettin, M. Sacco, C. Siniscalchi, H. W. Raeder, M. R. Weil, R. L. Stevens
nominations.abstract: Anti-cancer drug response prediction (DRP) is critically important for precision oncology and therapeutic development. Currently, most DRP models are developed using drug screening data from immortalized cancer cell lines, which can differ substantially from patient tumors at the genomic and molecular levels, even though patient tumor response is the ultimate prediction target. To help bridge this gap and bring DRP models closer to their intended clinical application, we conducted four drug screening studies using patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which more faithfully recapitulate patient tumors than immortalized cell lines. These studies generated data for improving and evaluating DRP models, including multi-omics profiles of PDO lines, drug feature data, and treatment response measurements. Using these data, we retrained and evaluated multiple publicly available DRP models under three model-building scenarios: training models using cell line data only, training models using combined cell line and PDO data, and pretraining models on cell line data followed by fine-tuning on PDO data. We then evaluated and compared model prediction performance on PDOs across these analysis scenarios. In addition, we also assessed the consistency of drug screening viability data generated by different laboratories using different assay technologies and/or experimental protocols.

nominations.title: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
nominations.authors: Simon Bur{\'e}, Jona Joachim, Florent Di Meglio
nominations.abstract: We propose an online method for choosing both a blood pressure target and a norepinephrine dose for an individual surgical patient. From a short record of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and norepinephrine delivery, the method fits a reduced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model and uses a local Gaussian approximation to propagate uncertainty to future MAP readings. It searches for the lowest target for which a bolus and constant infusion keep the predicted probability of at least one MAP reading below 65 mmHg after the rise phase within a prescribed limit. If no such target is found, the decision returns to the clinician. We assess calibration of the predicted minimum MAP on retrospective surgical records under the doses actually administered. In a cohort of 4,096 virtual patients, the method recommended a dose for 74 % of patients at a nominal risk of 5 %. Among the patients receiving a recommendation, 6.9 % had a reading below 65 mmHg. A fixed target of 70 mmHg yielded a rate of 25 % when applied to the full virtual cohort.

nominations.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
nominations.authors: Paarth Batra, Aryan Keluskar
nominations.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) produce highly accurate contact maps from single-sequence inputs. People often take this accuracy as proof that these models implicitly learn invariant coevolutionary statistics, extracting the same signals as classical alignment-based methods like Potts. In this work, we introduce a diagnostic framework around a global bijective relabeling of the amino-acid alphabet. This transformation permutes residue letters while leaving all alignment-level information, column entropies, and pairwise edit distances unchanged. Pseudolikelihood Potts models and inverse-covariance estimators remain invariant under this transformation, but pLMs fail the test. Across multiple architectures (ESM-2, MSA Transformer, AMPLIFY) and model scales (8M to 3B parameters), pLM contact maps collapse under arbitrary relabeling. Using Hamming distance controls and biochemical grouping interventions, we attempt to isolate what likely causes this degradation and find that these models rely on explicit, canonical residue identities (``alphabet anchoring'') rather than pure coevolutionary statistics. Increasing scale makes models more responsive to biochemical classes, but their performance still degrades under relabeling. Our findings show a gap between how pLMs and classical coevolutionary models compute contacts. More broadly, our work shows how diagnostic perturbations that leave classical models provably unchanged can expose hidden representation biases and prevent over-reliance on neural black boxes in biological modeling.

nominations.title: Deep Unrolling of Lanczos-based Laplacian Eigensolver for Crop Classification in Satellite Images
nominations.authors: Parham Eftekhar, Gene Cheung
nominations.abstract: Per-pixel crop classification in satellite images is an important pre-processing step in remote crop monitoring. Leveraging progress in signed graph signal processing, we build an interpretable and lightweight neural network for binary crop classification (e.g., corn versus non-corn) in two stages: i) learn a signed graph from data, and ii) unroll a Lanczos-based eigensolver to compute the eigenvector $\u_1$ associated with the smallest eigenvalue of a hybrid graph Laplacian $\cL$ for spectral clustering. Specifically, we first construct a near-balanced signed graph $\cG^s$, where signed edge weights $w_{i,j}\in(-1,1)$ are computed from learned feature distances $d_{i,j}$ via a hyperbolic tangent mapping. Given $\cG^s$, we estimate $\u_1$ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use $\mathrm{sign}(\u_1)$ for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which $\u_1$ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.

nominations.title: Joint Beamforming and Duplex-Mode Segment Selection for Secure Uplink Transmission in Pinching Antenna Systems
nominations.authors: Zar Chi Phyo, Mohamed Elhattab, Chadi Assi, Sanaa Sharafeddine
nominations.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have recently emerged as a promising architecture for reconfigurable, flexible and proximity-driven signal delivery. In this paper, we propose a segmented waveguide-based PASS architecture for enabling secure uplink communications, where each segment activates at most one pinching antenna (PA), which inherently eliminates the inter-antenna re-radiation effect and yields a tractable uplink signal model. To protect the uplink transmission against eavesdropping, the base station (BS) injects artificial noise (AN) toward the eavesdroppers via selected downlink segments using a duplex-mode segment selection mechanism, which dynamically configures each segment for either uplink reception or downlink AN transmission through switch-controlled fiber connections. We formulate the secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes the receive beamforming vector, AN covariance, user transmit power, pinching antenna positions, and duplex-mode segment assignment. Given the non-convex and combinatorial nature of the problem, we develop an efficient alternating optimization (AO) framework, where the resulting subproblems are solved using the Dinkelbach method combined with successive convex approximation (SCA) and penalty-based relaxation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of SEE and robustness against waveguide attenuation. Moreover, AN effectively suppresses information leakage, while PA mobility, duplex-mode segment allocation, and waveguide segmentation further improve secrecy performance through flexible positioning and reduced in-waveguide propagation loss.

nominations.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
nominations.authors: Joonas T\"orm\"al\"a, SaiKrishna Saketh Yellapragada, Eeli Susan, Esa Ollila
nominations.abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

nominations.title: Full-Duplex Communication for Pinching Antenna Systems
nominations.authors: Shaokang Hu, Ruotong Zhao, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Jinhong Yuan
nominations.abstract: This paper investigates multiuser full-duplex (FD) communication assisted by a multiwaveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) where each dielectric waveguide can be dynamically configured to operate in either downlink transmission or uplink reception mode. We develop a channel model that accounts for in-waveguide power attenuation and cumulative pinching antenna (PA)-induced phase shift. Building on this model, we jointly optimize the waveguide modes, PA locations, PA radiation/collection coefficients, downlink beamformers, uplink receive combiners, and uplink transmit powers to maximize the downlink weighted sum-rate (WSR) subject to uplink quality-of-service (QoS) requirements and power constraints. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonconvex resource allocation problem, we propose a low-complexity hierarchical block coordinate descent algorithm that capitalizes on weighted minimum mean-square error, fractional programming, majorization-minimization, and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to obtain a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed FD-PASS outperforms an FD base station equipped with fixed antennas and exhibits greater robustness against residual self-interference. Moreover, ignoring cumulative PA-induced phase shifts can produce QoS-infeasible designs.

nominations.title: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing With Pre-Chirp Spreading Index Modulation: A CSI-Driven Secure Transmission Framework
nominations.authors: Yiwei Tao, Miaowen Wen, Yao Ge, Merouane Debbah, Erdal Panayirci
nominations.abstract: The flexible configurability of pre-chirp parameters in affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) provides new degrees of freedom for designing covert communication mechanisms. Leveraging this property, this paper proposes a covert AFDM pre-chirp spreading index modulation (IM) framework referred to as AFDM-PCS-IM, tailored for high-mobility scenarios. Specifically, an orthogonal pre-chirp parameter codebook is constructed by exploiting the tunability of the pre-chirp parameters. To enhance covertness, the legitimate channel state information (CSI) is utilized to generate controlled perturbations that encrypt the codebook, thereby tightly coupling the modulation structure with instantaneous channel characteristics. The encrypted pre-chirp codebook is then employed as an IM dimension for information transmission, where the index bits are conveyed through the selection of pre-chirp parameter sequences. Since eavesdroppers cannot obtain consistent CSI, they are unable to reconstruct the encrypted codebook and thus cannot reliably recover any useful information. Moreover, to address channel estimation errors inherent in practical communication environments, a noise-aware CSI quantizer is further introduced to improve robustness under imperfect CSI conditions. Finally, a low-complexity two-layer message passing detector with Walsh code constraints (TLMP-WC) is developed to enable efficient large-scale data detection while simultaneously enhancing the detection reliability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AFDM-PCS-IM framework with the TLMP-WC detector achieves superior covertness, improved bit error rate (BER) performance, and reduced computational complexity compared with the state-of-the-art schemes.

nominations.title: Multi-Band Indoor MIMO Channel Measurements Across Sub-6 GHz, Mid-Band and mmWave: Comparing 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz
nominations.authors: Faruk Pasic, Florian Kiss, Florian Asperger, Diego Dupleich, Stefan Schwarz, Markus Rupp
nominations.abstract: Future wireless systems for indoor applications are expected to extend their operating frequencies from sub-6 GHz to mid-band and millimeter wave (mmWave) frequencies to support higher data rates. To characterize the frequency-dependent propagation behavior across these bands, multi-band channel measurements are essential. In this work, we conduct double-directional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel measurements in an indoor environment to enable a consistent comparison across three frequency bands. Measurements are performed using a 16x16 MIMO configuration at center frequencies of 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz, covering both line-of-sight (LOS) and obstructed line-of-sight (OLOS) conditions. The measured channels are processed using the space-alternating generalized expectation maximization (SAGE) algorithm to extract multipath parameters, which are subsequently used to characterize the angular power distributions across the three frequency bands. The results show substantial angular-domain similarity across all three bands in both LOS and OLOS conditions, while also highlighting frequency-dependent variations.

nominations.title: Multi-Label Classification with Constrained Search for Inverse Design of a 16x16 Reconfigurable Pixel Antenna
nominations.authors: Nadeem Rather, Holger Claussen, Lester Ho
nominations.abstract: In this paper, an inverse design method is presented for a 16x16 reconfigurable pixel antenna with 480 binary switches, giving 2480 possible patterns, far beyond what full-wave simulation can explore. Given a target frequency between 1 and 6 GHz, the method searches for a switch configuration whose simulated resonance lies close to the target. A forward surrogate model is trained on 22,152 full- wave simulated patterns to predict where a given switch pattern resonates. The forward task is formulated as multi-label classification over 100 frequency bins rather than reflection-coefficient regression, because a curve-fitting objective is dominated by the flat baseline around the narrow resonances of this structure. The inverse design is a simulated annealing search over the switch state, with a connectivity constraint maintained at every step so that every pattern generated is a valid antenna. The proposed methodology combines resonance-focused surrogate modelling with connectivity-constrained discrete optimization, enabling candidate generation without full-wave solver calls during the search. The pipeline is verified in CST Microwave Studio by simulating 220 predicted candidates, ten for each of 22 target frequencies. For each request, the best of the ten candidates reached a median frequency error of 23 MHz across the 22 targets, compared with 35 MHz for a solver-guided search using 200 simulations for each target. The proposed methodology therefore enables automatic switch configuration to achieve a requested resonant frequency, eliminating solver calls during the search and manual redesign of the antenna geometry.

nominations.title: Analytical Characterization of Radial Resolution at Oblique Angles for Near-Field Communications
nominations.authors: Viviana Centritto, Sotiris Droulias, Angeliki Alexiou
nominations.abstract: Exploiting radial resolvability in near-field communications requires analytical expressions that directly map physical beam parameters to resolution-controllable focal regions. However, beam characterization at oblique angles produces complex algebraic expressions that mask these critical interactions. In this work, we introduce an electromagnetic-aware analytical model built upon a tight upper bound of the spatial power density. This approach yields compact, closed-form solutions for the peak intensity position and radial focal extent, enabling the design of contiguous multi-user focal regions with controlled radial resolution. Performance evaluations confirm that the framework closely tracks exact solutions while facilitating system dimensioning and inter-beam interference management across varying steering angles.

nominations.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Optimization of Large Domino-Tiled Phased Arrays for Dual-Band LEO Satellite Communications
nominations.authors: Mohammad Mashayekhi, Gholamreza Askari
nominations.abstract: Irregular domino tiling reduces the number of transmit/receive modules (TRMs) of large phased arrays, but its design requires repeated pattern evaluations whose cost grows rapidly with aperture size. This paper presents a hybrid deep learning and optimization framework for large domino-tiled arrays. A local-flip Markov chain generator, about $5.2\times$ faster than a randomized greedy baseline, produces balanced tilings with nearly equal numbers of horizontal and vertical dominoes, and a Tabu Search engine reaches a sidelobe level (SLL) about $0.8$~dB lower than a genetic algorithm, simulated annealing, and iterated local search at comparable directivity. These tools build the dataset on which a convolutional neural network (CNN) surrogate is trained to predict, from the tiling structure alone, whether a candidate yields a favorable multi-angle SLL. Gating the Tabu Search with the surrogate removes $60.6$--$70.6\%$ of the full evaluations and speeds up the search by $2.56$--$3.80$ times for apertures from $20\times20$ to $100\times100$ elements, without degrading the solution quality. A convex amplitude--phase optimization of the fixed tilings then gives equal or higher directivity than two state-of-the-art methods at a comparable SLL, with more than an order of magnitude shorter computation time. Finally, the framework is applied to a $36\times36$ dual-band circularly polarized array for low Earth orbit (LEO) terminals at $11.2$ and $14.0$~GHz, whose bands are a factor of $1.25$ apart, using $648$ dominoes and a common element spacing selected from a sweep. The array scans to $50^\circ$ with no grating lobe and, compared with a reference irregular array, gives higher directivity over most of the scan range, a lower SLL at large scan angles, and a spacing that is more practical for the lower band.

nominations.title: Geometry-based Efficient Airy Beam Training for Quasi-LoS in Terahertz Near-field Communications
nominations.authors: Wenqi Zhao, Chong Han
nominations.abstract: With enlarged antenna apertures in Terahertz (THz) communications, near-field propagation becomes increasingly dominant, highlighting quasi-line-of-sight (quasi-LoS) scenarios with partial blockage. Airy beams offer a promising solution through their curved trajectories, but existing training methods for unknown blockage rely on computationally intensive parameter searches or learning-based approaches. In this paper, we propose an efficient geometry-based Airy beam training framework for uniform linear array (ULA) and uniform planar array (UPA) systems. First, theoretical feasibility bounds under finite apertures are derived to eliminate infeasible codewords. A performance-oriented Slope-Depth Geometric Codebook (SDGC) is then developed using bending-direction probing and geometric sampling. To further reduce training overhead, a latency-oriented Bijective 1D Geometric Codebook (B1GC) is proposed by mapping blockage-avoidance waypoints to receiver targets, enabling one-dimensional search. For UPA systems, a hybrid focusing--Airy mode is introduced, using four probe beams to identify the blockage-avoidance dimension and bending direction, followed by Airy beam training and orthogonal near-field focusing. Simulations show that SDGC achieves 14.8 bit/s/Hz average spectral efficiency with 40.9\% lower training overhead than the hierarchical focusing--Airy codebook (HFAC), while B1GC reduces overhead by 87.1\% with comparable performance. The UPA results further demonstrate effectiveness under two-dimensional blockage.

nominations.title: A Tutorial on Infrastructure Self-Calibration for Radio-Based Indoor Positioning
nominations.authors: Paul Schwarzbach
nominations.abstract: Radio positioning needs the positions of its anchors, access points, base stations, or reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, and manual surveying is costly and error-prone. Calibrating this infrastructure from its own measurements is one estimation problem, studied in at least four communities as self-calibration, auto-positioning, anchor self-localization, network localization, or radio simultaneous localization and mapping. This tutorial teaches the problem through one factor graph. The measurement topology sets its factors, the reference information enters as priors, and other measurement models add nuisance states. The tutorial shows what ranges can identify, from rigidity to the motion a mobile device must contribute, and presents multidimensional scaling, nonlinear least squares, recursive filters, and convex relaxations as inference engines over this graph. One session of a ten-anchor ultra-wideband deployment is carried through every step, and recordings from a second, harsher deployment and a public partial mesh serve as contrasts. The examples illustrate three lessons. On a full mesh, choose a robust loss and set its scale first, and calibrate with the engine of the positioning system, since the engines then reach similar errors. On thinned or partial meshes, test the result at surveyed check points, because the start decides which minimum a solver reaches. On a line-of-sight deployment, estimate range offsets, which lower the error floor that a systematic ranging bias sets and a robust loss cannot remove. A decision tree and a table of their effects turn them into deployment guidance. Code and result tables are openly released, and the data are published separately.

nominations.title: Over-the-Air Computation for Imperfectly Synchronized Multi-View Semantic Communication
nominations.authors: Maximilian H. V. Tillmann, Julian S\"undermann, Ahmad Halimi Razlighi, Edgar Beck, Armin Dekorsy
nominations.abstract: Compared to classical task-agnostic communication systems, which focus on reliable transmission of a message, semantic communication (SemCom) focuses on transmitting the task-relevant meaning behind the message. In this paper, we design a SemCom system for a distributed multi-view scenario, where multiple semantic devices observe a scene and collaborate through a single semantic receiver to execute a task. We propose adopting an Over-the-Air Computation (AirComp) channel for efficient use of resources, as AirComp uses a superposition of signals to directly compute a function, which in SemCom is decoding the semantic variable. However, AirComp relies heavily on perfect time and phase synchronization, which is not practical in real-world communication. We show that timing offsets of standards like 5G cause negligible degradation, and that larger timing offsets can be compensated by training. Nevertheless, the system cannot deal with the encountered levels of phase synchronization errors, even when trained with those levels of synchronization errors. Therefore, we propose integrating existing phase synchronization algorithms into the AirComp SemCom system training. Simulation results show that the proposed system can approach the task execution performance of a perfectly synchronized SemCom system.

nominations.title: A Proof-of-Concept Study of Wi-Fi Channel State Information-Based Fall Detection Using ESP32 Devices
nominations.authors: Amritha S. S., Anhajul S. Rahman, Mohammed Bin Saleem, Vaishnav Sankar, Jerrin Thomas Panachakel
nominations.abstract: This paper reports a small-scale proof-of-concept study of contactless fall detection using Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) collected with two ESP32 devices. One device acts as the transmitter and the other as the receiver, with a separation of 3.5~m. The evaluated signal-processing pipeline uses CSI amplitude, second-level discrete wavelet transform (DWT) denoising with a Symlet-10 wavelet, z-score normalization, and fixed-length segmentation. Wavelet-scattering coefficients are used as features, and MATLAB's automated classifier-selection workflow identifies a LogitBoost ensemble with a minimum leaf size of four and a learning rate of 0.022052. The proposed classifier achieved an accuracy of 93.10%, with a precision of 100%, recall of 87.50%, and F1-score of 93.33%. These results demonstrate the potential of Wi-Fi CSI-based sensing for contactless fall detection using low-cost ESP32 hardware.

nominations.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
nominations.authors: Jochen Fink, Renato L. G. Cavalcante, S{\l}awomir Sta\'nczak
nominations.abstract: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.

nominations.title: Physics-Informed Generative Augmentation for Open-Set UAV Classification
nominations.authors: Michel Kulhandjian, Levon Aslanyan
nominations.abstract: Open-set recognition of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from passive 5G radar micro-Doppler signatures is challenging because unknown drone types cannot be anticipated at training time. We propose a physics-informed generative adversarial network (PI-GAN) that conditions spectrogram synthesis on rotor kinematics, forcing the classifier's feature space to encode physically meaningful structure. We compare PI-GAN augmentation against a vanilla conditional GAN (CGAN) and basic data augmentation across three held-out configurations with 1, 2, and 3 unknown classes. Vanilla CGAN augmentation collapses open-set clustering, reducing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) from 0.97 to 0.01, whereas PI-GAN preserves it at 0.97. In a controlled held-out sweep with two unknown classes, PI-GAN achieves an ARI of 0.92 compared to 0.07 for vanilla CGAN. The physics-informed features enable unsupervised separation of mechanically distinct unknown drones without retraining, demonstrating that physics-conditioned generation is the key enabler of open-set capability.

nominations.title: A Four-Branch Radar Target Simulator with Fractional Delay on a PlutoSDR
nominations.authors: Florian Euchner, Stephan ten Brink
nominations.abstract: Repeatable test setups support the development and evaluation of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) hardware and algorithms. Commercial radar target simulators are expensive, while sub-6 GHz ISAC experiments often need only tens of megahertz of bandwidth within their available spectrum allocation. This makes simpler, low-cost test hardware attractive. We present a low-cost, open-source radar target simulator based on an ADALM-Pluto without hardware modification, supporting four independently configurable targets and analog bandwidths up to 56 MHz. The FPGA generates echoes with independent delays, Doppler shifts and gains, using fractional-delay filters for sub-sample adjustment. For motion-consistent echoes, delay and carrier phase are updated together to reproduce both changing range and frequency-dependent Doppler shifts. Over-the-air measurements demonstrate simultaneous echoes, sub-sample delay adjustment, and smooth target motion between sample positions. The FPGA source, firmware and on-device web interface are publicly available.

nominations.title: Reliable Near-Field Source Enumeration and Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC
nominations.authors: Jiaying Li, Haifeng Wen, Changsheng You, Yuanwei Liu, Hong Xing
nominations.abstract: Accurate and reliable near-field multi-source localization is essential for location-aware processing in future wireless systems. However, coherent multipath propagation complicates the direct recovery of line-of-sight (LoS) source positions, while existing estimation methods generally lack explicit control of the risk of source underestimation and positioning uncertainty. In this paper, we investigate reliable source enumeration and positioning in near-field coherent multipath environments. Specifically, we develop a conformal risk control (CRC) based source enumeration scheme that calibrates the penalty coefficient of an eigenvalue-based criterion to control the expected miss-detection ratio at a prescribed level. We further propose MUSIC-Net, a model-based deep learning framework informed by two-stage MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC), which learns the LoS-related subspace and surrogate distances through subspace-distance-based training, thereby enabling direct source positioning without estimating non-line-of-sight (NLoS) path parameters or performing subsequent path association. To quantify the uncertainty of the estimated positions, we develop a split conformal prediction (SCP) based calibration method that constructs angle-range predicted regions with finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantees. Numerical results show that the proposed framework effectively controls the risk of source underestimation, while providing improved positioning accuracy with tighter predicted regions than benchmarks given the same target coverage levels.

nominations.title: Rule-Sensitive Sensor Participation in Distributed Detection with Prescribed Boolean Fusion Rules
nominations.authors: Ahmad Tanha
nominations.abstract: We study distributed binary detection when the fusion node must implement a prescribed Boolean decision rule. Under conditionally independent Bernoulli observations, we derive a signed-influence path identity valid for arbitrary Boolean rules; for monotone rules, it reduces to an exact Russo--Margulis representation in terms of coordinate influences. The identity yields rule-sensitive necessary conditions for a target Bayes error and an influence-weighted Kullback--Leibler feasibility bound. We then connect Boolean relevance to exact rule implementation and derive lower bounds on the number of sensors that must participate, including a heterogeneous bound based on the ordered per-sensor hypothesis separations. Numerical and Monte Carlo results illustrate both the tightening provided by the heterogeneous participation bound and the performance penalty that can arise when a prescribed fusion rule is retained instead of optimal likelihood-ratio fusion.

nominations.title: The BEATS Dataset: Towards Understanding Music-Physiology Dynamics in Real-World Scenarios
nominations.authors: Benjamin Gutierrez Serafin, Tanaya Guha, Fahim Kawsar
nominations.abstract: We introduce the BEATS dataset, a robust compilation of psycho-physiological data collected in the wild from 30 participants while they listened to curated playlists intended to promote well-being. An acronym for Biomarkers, Experience and Affect from Therapeutic Soundscapes, the BEATS dataset aims to support research on wellbeing, music psychology, affective computing and signal processing. More specifically, this dataset includes: (1) sensor data collected during music listening sessions using a research-grade wearable device in free-movement environments; (2) music listening activity records, stimulus metadata, acoustic features, and self-reports associated with the listening sessions (3) individual characteristics, such as demographics, music preference, musical skills, and personality traits; and (4) self-reported psychological measures before and after their experimental participation spanning for a number of weeks. By situating data collection outside of lab settings, the BEATS dataset offers the opportunity to study real-world music-listening scenarios, allowing for a richer exploration of the physiological, subjective and therapeutic effects of music under real-world conditions.

nominations.title: NORA: Neuro-headstage for Online Recording and Actuation in Freely Behaving Animal Models
nominations.authors: Savanna Blade, Yuhan Hou, He Jia, Laura Kondrataviciute, Runtian Yang, Suneil K. Kalia, Xilin Liu
nominations.abstract: This paper presents NORA, a compact wireless neuro-headstage designed for simultaneous neural recording and stimulation in freely behaving animal models. Separate recording and stimulation interfaces, each managed with a dedicated MCU and wireless module, are integrated into a fully head-mounted device compatible with standard Omnetics connectors; this separation allows for simultaneous recording and stimulation without sample-dropping or stimulation waveform distortion. To minimize stimulation artifacts and cross-domain interference, the recording and stimulation subsystems are electrically isolated with independent power domains and dedicated wireless communication paths. NORA has been validated through in vivo animal experiments, demonstrating acquisition of meaningful neural features with results comparable to a commercial wireless headstage. Together, these features establish a practical platform for artifact-reduced neuromodulation research.

nominations.title: Circuit-aware protection against burst errors in lattice surgery
nominations.authors: Jaebum Kim
nominations.abstract: Large-scale quantum computing will require logical operations protected against high-energy impacts that disturb many superconducting qubits at once. Gap engineering suppresses relaxation induced by these impacts, but protecting only a subset of qubits requires choosing where that protection is placed. During lattice surgery, measurements change as patches merge and split, exposing different ancillas and temporal boundaries to burst errors. Here we compare three static protection layouts for a simulated lattice-surgery CNOT, matching the numbers of protected ancillas and the X:Z check-type splits. At distance 9, protecting the check type measured during each merge reduces burst-induced excess risk by $38^{+6}_{-5}\%$ relative to a deep geometric band under correlated background matching, without giving the decoder the impact parameters. We attribute this difference to report errors at temporal boundaries and ancilla faults propagating to data, which interact to increase the excess risk of a shallow band. We also find that the typed layout reaches the shallow-band reference risk with an estimated $49^{+2}_{-14}$ fewer protected ancillas. At distance 13, the advantage is not resolved under oracle decoding, and a five-round burst cap reverses the shallow-band ordering.
